cards.anchor: N1 is recognized yet pending through boundary 3. This defeats the account that every bulk-selected pending identity represents outstanding recognition demand; registration eligibility and distinct recognition remain valuable.
cards.burden: Registration clerk validates six notices in six ticks. Dispatcher spends six actions, selecting five individual identities and timing one bulk request; this displaces routine bulk selection into explicit scheduling. Readable ledgers require no added clerk labor. No role exchange or extra capacity is assumed.
cards.construction: Register N3,N4,N5,N6,N7,N8 at ticks 0,1,2,3,4,5 respectively. Dispatch individual N2 at 0, N3 at 1, N4 at 2; idle at 3; bulk at 4 selects N5,N6 after N1 clears; individual N7 at 5 and N8 at 6. Idle thereafter.
cards.defeat: Reject if replay fails to produce eight registrations and eight distinct recognitions by boundary 9 within six actions, or if the boundary-4 bulk includes another identity. A changed display, eligibility or FIFO rule would invalidate this construction.
cards.mutation: Attack early bulk dependence without abolishing bulk: target three early unrecognized identities, retain one batch after the exceptional display clears, then target the two later registrations.
cards.prediction_candidate: Model prediction: new first successes N2,N3,N4,N5,N6,N7,N8 occur at ticks 1,2,3,5,6,7,8. Tick 4 is empty. All registrations complete by boundary 6; including initial N1, recognition reaches eight by boundary 9. No duplicate or failure occurs.
cards.prediction_rival: Model prediction: initial bulk adds N1 before N2. N1 duplicates at tick 1; N4 remains pending at boundary 4 and is batched again, duplicating at tick 5. N7 succeeds at 8, leaving N8 queued beyond the window: eight registrations, seven recognitions.
cards.probe: Replay both schedules from the stipulated initial state, logging registration completion, request identity and eligibility, boundary dashboard, FIFO delivery, duplicates and distinct recognitions. Compare boundary-9 counts and six-action totals; verify N8 delivery at an available tick.
cards.rival: Use the identical registration sequence and dispatcher timing, replacing only individual N2 at tick 0 with routine bulk. Keep individual N3 at 1, N4 at 2, bulk at 4, N7 at 5 and N8 at 6.
unknowns: Later sender adaptation is unobserved and is not present demand.
Replay tests this finite model; empirical network behavior and global schedule optimality remain unestablished.
